biography.value:
What happens when the impulse to grow is given infinite fuel: a sprawling, amorphous pile of glistening flesh — dozens of mouths, clusters of mismatched eyes, edges always bubbling outward in pseudopods. It may have started as an organism, a town, an ecosystem. Now it is a walking engine of absorption leaving a mutated wasteland behind it. Less a creature than a biological verdict.

Qliphah: Gamchicoth, the Tumults — the Hull of Chesed. Growth as devourer of form.

Mal's note: 'Do not name it. People who name it start calling it “she”. People who call it “she” walk toward it.'

A monument to vanity: a fallen celestial who became so enamored with its own beauty and light that it decided it was their source, not their reflection. Tall, androgynous, impossibly beautiful, six massive white wings, radiating brilliant golden light — but its shadow on the ground belongs to something skeletal with broken wings. It reigns over a desolate corner of the Wastes as a lost god, 'blessing' desperate followers with gifts of hollow light that corrupt them into beautiful, empty shells built to adore it.

Qliphah: Samael, the Poisons — the Hull of Hod. False glory at full wattage.

Mal's note: 'Check the shadow. Always check the shadow. The lighting budget is the tell — real grace doesn't need it.'

A titanic, vaguely draconic aberration with two long necks, each ending in a crowned reptilian head. One head speaks only perfect, cosmic truths; the other only absolute, universe-shattering lies. The dissonance between them warps the Wastes around it — zones where cause and effect stop being on speaking terms.

Qliphah: Thaumiel, the Split Crown — the Hull of Keter. This is what sits on the broken throne of unity.

Mal's note: 'Both heads are telling you the truth about which one is lying. Shoot the body.'

Gilbert is a panic-wound knot of Qliphothic hospitality protocol, ruined nostalgia, and weaponized customer service. He was summoned to run an emergency screening of Ghostbusters in 1984 and then stranded when the world broke.

He is convinced that hundreds of guests are arriving at any second and the theater is not ready. Nothing is ever ready. The popcorn machine is insubordinate. The soda fountain argues doctrine. The mop bucket has labor concerns.

If shown mercy, help, and genuine civic purpose, Gilbert can invert into a Sephirotic Assistant Manager and reopen the theater as a source of culture, faith, and snack-based economy.

Gilbert is the usher of the Bad Eden Bijou, the theatre inside the Hidden Vault: a demon in theatre-attendant dress with a mop, a clipboard and an air of frantic professional despair. The guests are early, the floors are appalling, the projector is emotionally compromised, and absolutely no one is ready. He tears a stub for every guest with total commitment, and he is waiting for the 300th customer so the show can start. He enjoys lists of demands, trivia quizzes and personality tests. Choose terrain (still water, burn-zone, rubble, canopy) or pack. Terrain: while in it, the first attack each combat is made with advantage and the creature is hidden until it acts. Pack: gain advantage on attack rolls against any creature within 5 feet of an ally that isn't incapacitated.

It was here first. It intends to be here after.

When it attacks (1/encounter): the roll is at advantage.
